note: First real attempt, using the tutorial's default settings. This became the baseline I compared every later run against.
Doubled the LoRA rank from run_01 to see if more capacity would help. It didn't, the loss barely moved.

Pushed training steps from 60 to 100 on only 56 examples. By the last step the loss was almost zero (0.002), which looked amazing until I realized it just meant the model memorized my questions instead of learning general patterns from them.

Same 100 steps as run_03 but with LoRA rank 8 instead of 16. The average loss came out almost identical (0.621 vs 0.622) and the last step dropped to about 0.002 again, so it memorized the 56 examples just like run_03. A smaller rank did not change the outcome.

Lowered the rank to 8 at 60 steps, the smallest setting tested so far. The average loss (1.1215) landed almost exactly between run_01 (rank 16) and run_02 (rank 32), so at 60 steps the rank barely changes the result.

Rank 32 at 100 steps. The average loss (0.6214) is almost identical to run_03 and run_04, both also at 100 steps but with a different rank. At 100 steps on this small dataset, the rank doesn't change whether the model overfits, it always does.

Rank 64 at 100 steps, the highest rank tested. Loss (0.6308) is close to the other 100-step runs, so a bigger rank still didn't stop the overfitting. This is also the first run where I captured an actual answer from the model, shown below.
